idiom_name: one serialized column + codec + mapping hook + version tag
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: pick a codec (JSON, CBOR/Protobuf/FlatBuffers, or a private TLV format), fix the payload contract, and bind it to a single BLOB/BYTEA or JSON/JSONB column through the persistence layer's type-mapping hook. Keep the primary key, the version/optimistic-lock token and every filtered field as ordinary columns; the payload is one atomic datum, so its size is a design constraint. Prefix the payload with a format version (or configure the codec's own versioning) and write the reader so it can handle - or explicitly reject - every version still present in the table. Prefer text/JSON codecs when the engine offers JSON operators, and reserve native object serialization for private, trusted payloads.
code_sketch:
row:  id | version | payload (BLOB / JSON / JSONB) | updated_at

save: payload = codec.encode(entity)        # starts with a format-version tag
      bind(column, payload)                 # one row, one statement
load: entity = codec.decode(payload)        # unknown version -> explicit error
pitfalls: Skipping the version tag makes the first field rename unrecoverable.
Leaving identity or the optimistic-lock token inside the payload breaks row addressing and conflict detection.

Wrong move: mutate the decoded payload in place and expect the ORM to notice -> the column is one opaque value, dirty checking sees no change and issues no UPDATE -> reassign a fresh copy of the payload to the attribute (or hook mutation explicitly: SQLAlchemy MutableDict/flag_modified, Hibernate @Entity on a mutable type or a new instance per write).

Wrong move: filter JSON paths inside the payload assuming the column type makes them indexed -> every query scans and parses whole documents -> add a GIN/expression index over exactly the queried paths, or promote the filtered fields to real columns.

Wrong move: persist with language-native object serialization (Java Serializable, .NET BinaryFormatter) because it is one line of code -> a class rename, package move or library bump makes existing rows unreadable, and loading column bytes instantiates whatever classes the payload names (CWE-502) -> use a schema-driven text/binary codec with an explicit version tag and, if native serialization is unavoidable, an allowlist of deserializable classes.
